Identity contract: Four removable structural panels assemble around a central tensioned core to alternate between rigid briefcase and flat-folder states. Panels slide on and are tensioned by the central core rather than folding as a conventional soft bag. The product remains a functional bag/briefcase capable of carrying and protecting contents. All four functional panels must engage one real central structural core and support reversible rigid and flat states. Approved redesign: Use four exceptionally thin goatskin planes with controlled shadow gaps and softened precision corners. Expose the central core only at top and base interfaces through refined tension hardware. Use a tall, slim architectural brief in deep electric blue with restrained white edge punctuation. Express strong proportions, material credibility, controlled novelty, intentional color, visual hierarchy, restraint, and plausible premium execution. The structural mechanism must remain operative and recognizable, never a decorative imitation. Do not change category, merge concepts, substitute a conventional product, or claim validated manufacturability or commercial readiness. One coherent product; no logos or text.
Variation 1 — architectural_clarity: Make the evaluated mechanism immediately legible through a disciplined, architectural silhouette and controlled luxury proportions.
Render one coherent product only, with no logos, captions, or text.
